root.name: Scotch Game: Tartakower Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. Nd2

overview: In the Schmidt Scotch after 5.Nxc6 bxc6 White plays 6.Nd2, a quieter move than 6.e5, covering e4 and heading for Nc4 or Bd3 and O-O. Black has doubled c-pawns but a broad centre and easy piece play with ...d5 or ...d6. White keeps a slight lead in space while Black relies on the bishop pair and the b-file.

white_ideas.idea: Keep e4 defended with Nd2 and reroute to c4 or f3
Develop Bd3 and castle, then play e5 at the right moment

black_ideas.idea: Use the half-open b-file and keep the c-pawns flexible

typical_structures.structure: White e4 against Black doubled c-pawns

character.notes: Quiet middlegame with small edges rather than direct attacks.

gambit.notes: Material is level after the knight trade on c6.

soundness.notes: A sound sideline with no refutation.

structure.notes: White e4 pawn against a Black centre that can open with ...d5.

approach.notes: A sideline of the Scotch that strong players choose now and then.

level.notes: Little forcing theory; the plan depends on handling the doubled pawns.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.e5 main Schmidt
sublines_that_differ.how: A sharper separate line, not the Tartakower

character.reason: Quiet development with doubled pawns for Black and no forcing play.

structure.reason: The centre is tense with ...d5 still to come.

approach.reason: Within the Scotch but a respectable sideline.

level.reason: Plans matter more than memorised lines.

plans.reason: Black has doubled c-pawns for central control.
